abilities.name: Assemble and maintain a simple shelter
abilities.function: Build a low single-person braced lean-to with a sloping bark roof from owned branches, vines and bark at a clear site; inspect, repair or dismantle it, or resume or cancel unfinished work.
abilities.costs: Study: 4 rounds. Start: x, y, orientation (degrees; 0 points the low roof edge toward increasing x, where wind comes from) and materials as exact owned, untreated whole units totalling 13 branch, 4 vine and 6 bark; stand within reach of a 2 m x 2 m footprint of ordinary dry soil that is inside the world, unobstructed and unoccupied. Twelve paid increments, one round and 1 energy each: 2 posts, 3 ridge and braces, 3 ribs and binding, 3 roofing courses, 1 final check; start pays the first and the same action continues each round. Resume pays the next increment of the unfinished work; cancel takes one round and no energy. Inspect: target in reach, one round, 0.2 energy. Repair (builder only): target, increment 1-11 and the exact replacement units of that increment, one round, 1 energy. Dismantle (builder only): target, one round and 1 energy per stage, removing the last installed stage. Gathering, travel and probe tests are separate actions with their own costs.
abilities.effects: Reserved materials stay carried and owned until each paid increment moves them into the structure as installed parts with the same quantity, origin and age; nothing is created or used up. After the final stability, binding, roof-load and runoff checks the shelter is commissioned: a 2 m x 1 m covered floor under a 1.2 m ridge and a roof sloping about 50 degrees. While exactly one person lies wholly on that floor in rain and wind up to 0.8, it removes up to 50% of the rain part and up to 35% of the wind part of the existing outdoor exposure chill, scaled by roof condition, by the share of the body under the roof along the wind-driven rain, and for wind by how directly the low edge faces the wind; wind entering the open side, stronger weather, water pooling on the floor or a second person gives no protection. Air temperature, hunger, nutrition and rest are unchanged, and copies never stack. A frame without its three roofing courses gives no rain protection. Each round installed parts wear by 0.0005 + 0.002 x rain + 0.002 x wind; a part below condition 0.5 makes a commissioned shelter unsafe with no protection until repair and a passing reinspection. Repair restores only the replaced parts; removed and dismantled parts return to the ground at the site with their condition and can be reused at that condition. Work not continued in a round pauses; a lost reserved material stops it. Cancel returns uninstalled materials once and leaves installed parts as an unfinished structure; death stops the work, drops uninstalled materials where the person died and leaves installed parts. No reward, mastery or refund.

Changes in who lies on each bay floor are reported. Repair restores only the replaced parts; removed and dismantled parts return to the ground at the bay with their condition and can be reused. abilities.name: Establish and tend a cultivation trial
abilities.function: Plant one owned, unspoiled meadow-root unit from a living root plant in a small hand-prepared soil position, where it can establish as a new root plant under the existing plant rules; observe trial positions or plant sources, take back what remains, or resume or cancel unfinished planting.
abilities.costs: Study: 2 rounds. Establish: inputStackId names one whole owned, untreated, unspoiled root unit (quantity 1) gathered from a living root plant (target, if given, must be that plant); x, y name a 0.25 m position within reach (0.65 m plus body radius) on ordinary meadow soil (.) inside the world, not standing water, waterlogging at most 0.1, soil moisture 0.3-1.2, at least 0.6 m from any object and clear of people, with fewer than 3 root plants or unfinished trials within 5 m. Three paid stages of one round and 1 energy each: prepare the position, place the unit, cover and record; establish pays the first and the same action continues each round. Resume pays the next stage after rechecking reach, site, unit and energy; cancel takes one round and no energy; processId selects the work. Observe: target a trial position or a plant source in reach, one round and 0.2 energy (the baseline probe observation). Remove (planter only): target in reach, one round and 1 energy. Tend has no supported intervention yet and is refused at no cost. Harvest uses gather at its own cost. No tool, water, fertilizer or seed is provided.
abilities.effects: The unit stays carried, owned and ageing until the placing stage moves it, with its origin, mass and age, out of the inventory into the position; then it cannot be eaten or planted elsewhere. Covering makes the position a planted root propagule under the existing plant rules: it gains establishment only from actual temperature, light, soil moisture and season, so cold, darkness, drought or waterlogging stall it, and if the buried unit spoils under the existing ageing law first, the trial dies. When establishment completes the unit becomes a new root plant (it leaves the food stocks) with no stock and a stock ceiling of at most 4, regrowing under the same growth rule as natural root plants and harvested by anyone only through gather; nothing is copied, reset or guaranteed. After 80 planted rounds without establishing or dying the trial reports an inconclusive status and continues. Observe records only visible stage, stock, soil and weather as an unverified personal record; repeated probe observations follow the existing evidence rules. Work not continued in a round pauses; too little energy, leaving reach or a changed site pauses without charge; a lost or spoiled unit stops the work. Cancel returns an unplaced unit once and leaves a placed unit uncovered in the position, where it does not establish. Death drops an unplaced unit where the person died and leaves placed or planted units to the ecology. Remove returns a placed or covered unit in its current condition, nothing for a dead trial, never an established plant, and clears the position. No reward, milestone or refund.

Inspect: target a visible object or item in reach (your own carried items count), one round and 0.2 energy (the baseline probe observation; no second charge), no material used. Separation-trial: target your own carried fallen-branch stack, one round and 0.5 energy on exactly 0.1 unit split off from it. Recover: target your own carried fallen-branch stack and quantity (0.1 steps, default all); needs your own earlier trial on material from the same source. Work is one increment per round of at most 0.1 m2 of bark surface at 1 energy each, including a smaller final increment (one branch unit carries about 0.18 m2); recover pays the first and the same action continues each round; resume pays the next increment; cancel takes one round and no energy. Hand only: a toolId is refused at no cost. Travel and gathering are separate actions.
abilities.effects: Represented composition (stated assumptions): one untreated fallen-branch unit (1.1 mass) is 0.99 wood and 0.11 attached bark (the bark-extraction@1 share), bark covers about 0.18 m2 at the bark unit basis of 0.3 mass per 0.5 m2, on a 2 m piece of about 0.09 m circumference, and separates by hand from the broken ends. Other materials have no represented bark composition: inspection reports them as unresolved and trial and recovery are refused at no cost. Inspect records only visible facts as a personal unverified record: bark covering, exposed edges, piece length, circumference, covered, separated and torn areas; attached mass and separability stay unknown until your own trial. The trial lifts and tears the bark of the 0.1 portion (recorded waste, about 0.011 mass) and reports edge, separation behaviour and bark share; the portion keeps its wood as its own stack. Each recover increment detaches real attached bark: every whole 0.03-mass tenth becomes ordinary carried bark (resource bark, same origin and harvest date, no other record), usable wherever bark units are used; a remainder below a tenth is recorded waste. The worked portion stays branch whose mass per unit falls by exactly the bark removed (0.99 when bare) and carries a separation record, so the shelters, which take only untreated units, do not accept it. Wood, attached bark, recovered bark and waste always sum to the input. Only the selected portion is reserved; it stays carried. Work not continued in a round pauses; too little energy pauses without spending; lost or changed material stops the work. Cancel returns the remainder in its actual state; death drops it on the ground. Completed products, damage, time and energy are never refunded. No shelter, comfort, food, regrowth or reward follows from separation.

Reviewed Ivo's round-4 request 'Prepare a substantial meal' and the World Agent's develop review (learning 1): the smallest general food-preparation operation, cold hand portioning and combining of already edible owned food without heat or equipment, with nutrition unchanged by preparation, eating left to the existing eat path and experience policy, and no stacked rewards. The existing prepare-food@1 (ex11 scope) is a different transformation (hand-mashing into averaged portions with a mass-based work rule and learning 2) and collective-material-combine@1 (ex12 scope) excludes food, so neither is an equivalent; their infrastructure is reused instead. Implemented food-preparation@1 in scope long-ex15 with modes start, resume and cancel and the single preparation cold-combine. Start takes 1-24 exact owned, unreserved {itemId, quantity} allocations in 0.1 steps of one food; each must be unspoiled, untreated and actually edible, and the person's own food record must show it as edible with toxicity 0. Work equals the selected quantity at one food unit per round and one energy per unit worked (Ivo's 3 berries take 3 rounds and 3 energy; a final partial unit costs its fraction); start pays the first increment, the same request continues each round, resume pays the next increment after revalidating every reserved ingredient (present, full quantity, unspoiled) and energy, and too little energy pauses without spending. At start the selected quantities move through the existing collective-work escrow into a reserved, carried, owned in-progress portion that keeps origin, harvest date and decay and keeps ageing; a round without paid work pauses the process. Completion atomically replaces the escrow with one carried stack of the same food (resource unchanged, same quantity and mass) whose original lots are kept as flat componentLots through material-lots.ts, so it eats exactly like the raw food through eat (same nutrition and toxicity per unit, eat's energy cost and satiety cap, partial eating debits those lots), each lot spoils under the existing rule with no shelf-life reset, and the meal-experience record (substantialNutrition 8, mealWindow 10) uses the same food, method and realized nutrition as eating it raw (quality from the oldest lot's decay), which deduplicates raw and prepared forms. A lost or spoiled reserved ingredient stops the work and returns the survivors in their current condition; cancel returns the remaining reserved food in its current condition without refunding energy or time; death stops the work and leaves the unfinished food on the ground once. Events: food-preparation-started, -progress, -paused, -resumed, -cancelled, -failed and -completed (the last names the output item, nominal nutrition 24 and toxicity 0 for Ivo's batch) carry actor, work id, actual input references and quantities, position, progress and tick; the job state is kept in the person's long:work:food-preparation state, and job and output carry visual metadata (component prepared-food, mode cold-combined, state, progress, quantity, ingredient shares and palette); no viewer component is added, so nothing draws a bowl, utensil, fire or steam. Modeling assumptions: hands are not represented, so a living person is treated as having usable hands; one food per batch only, because the existing eat debits component lots in order and no consistent per-portion mixture rule is represented, so mixing berries with roots is rejected rather than averaged; inputs with another represented treatment (water composition, drying, layers, equipment or other processing) are rejected; known safety means the person's own discovery record with toxicity 0; the prepared stack keeps the ingredient's resource and meal method 'unprocessed', since no washing, cutting, heating or other physical change occurs; the completion event is the practice evidence but is never qualified, so preparing earns no milestone, pleasure or other reward and any satisfaction comes only from the existing eat policy; cancel costs no energy. Reuse: collective-work.ts (allocations, escrow, paid work, stop), material-lots.ts (conserved component lots, refresh without rejuvenation), collective-food-profile.ts, the forest eat path, forest-experience meal policy and the forest decay loop, all unchanged; no other experiment changes because only the new long-ex15 package and its registration were added. This is a simplified real mechanism, not a first release: the specification is self-consistent and every cost and effect is implemented with real energy, time, material and events; mixed-food meals and heated, wet or tool-based modes are reported as not represented.

Reviewed Lin's round-8 request 'Construct a simple weather shelter' and the World Agent's develop review (learning 4): a general 'Assemble and maintain a simple shelter' operation for a low single-person braced lean-to with a sloping roof (two forked posts, a ridge pole, four braces, six ribs, 12 m of binding, 3 m2 of overlapping roofing, at most 2 m2 of covered floor, ridge at most 1.2 m, slope at least 35 degrees), 12 paid increments at 1 energy each, partial rain and wind shielding of at most 50% and 35% for one occupant within light-weather limits, weather wear, inspection, repair, dismantling, cancellation and death rules, and no new experience reward. Registry reconciliation: the complete long-ex15 registry (19 abilities: foundation-forest, foundation-open, foundation-expression and food-preparation@1) has no construction or shelter ability; the earlier shelter packages (resting-shelter@1 ex10, weather-lean-to@1 ex11, weather-barrier@1 ex14) are scoped to other experiments, so none is installed or duplicated; gather, probe, pickup, learn and navigation remain the separate existing operations. Unlike ex14's weather-barrier@1 first release, the specification is self-consistent, so this is a simplified but real mechanism, not a first release. Implemented simple-shelter@1 in scope long-ex15 with modes start, resume, cancel, inspect, repair and dismantle. Start takes x, y, orientation and exact owned untreated whole units totalling 13 branch, 4 vine and 6 bark, checks a 2 m x 2 m footprint (in reach, inside the world, ordinary '.' soil, waterlogging at most 0.1, no hazard, no overlap with solid or reserved objects, no living person), and reserves the materials through collective-work escrow as carried, owned pieces split per increment. Each paid increment (one round, 1 energy; start pays the first, the bound action continues) revalidates reach, reserved pieces, site waterlogging and occupancy, then moves that increment's pieces out of the stacks into persistent structure components with the same quantity, origin and age: 2 posts, 3 ridge and braces, 3 ribs and binding, 3 roofing courses of 2 bark, and a final increment that runs coded lateral-stability, binding-pull, roof-load and runoff checks; passing commissions the shelter and records the light-weather limits and the supported roof load (8.4 mass units), failing leaves it unverified. Too little energy, leaving reach, waterlogging or another occupant pause without charge; a round not worked pauses; a lost reserved piece stops the work and returns the survivors. Cancel (one round, no energy) returns uninstalled pieces once and leaves installed parts as an unfinished structure; death drops uninstalled pieces where the person died and leaves installed parts. Inspect (anyone who studied; one round, 0.2 energy) records an unverified personal record and reruns the checks, which can withdraw or restore protection. Repair (builder only; one round, 1 energy) replaces exactly one installed increment's parts with the same recipe of owned units, leaving the removed parts on the ground with their condition, and restores only those parts; protection lost to wear returns only after a passing reinspection. Dismantle (builder only; one round, 1 energy per stage) returns the last installed stage to the ground at the site with each part's condition; recovered parts can be reused at that condition. Effect: a new physiology hook (long-shelter-exposure.ts, inserted after the existing refuge and lean-to hooks in forest-environment.ts and inactive unless simple-shelter@1 is installed, so ex7-ex14 are unchanged) adds back exposure x (rain x rainShield + wind x windShield) of the existing outdoor exposure chill for exactly one living person wholly on the 2 m x 1 m covered floor of a commissioned shelter, with rainShield = 0.5 x roof condition x the body share whose wind-slanted rain ray meets the roof plane and windShield = 0.35 x roof condition x max(0, cos(orientation)); the body temperature then evolves through the existing update. Weather above 0.8 rain or wind, water pooling on the floor, a second person, the open side facing the wind, an unfinished, unverified or unsafe structure, or an enclosure already removing the chill give no protection; copies never stack; air temperature, hunger, nutrition and rest are unchanged. Each round installed parts wear by 0.0005 + 0.002 x rain + 0.002 x wind (the ex11 weather-lean-to law); a part below condition 0.5 makes a commissioned shelter unsafe. Events: simple-shelter-started, -progress, -paused, -resumed, -cancelled, -failed, -test-failed, -commissioned, -inspected, -deteriorated, -damaged, -repaired, -dismantled and -exposure-measured, all carrying the structure or work id; the structure's data.view holds reusable drawing metadata (component shelter, footprint, covered floor, orientation, slope, ridge height, installed components with resource colors and condition, roof coverage, stage, visible damage, status). No satisfaction rule, practice milestone (the commissioning event carries no qualified flag) or other reward is added. Modeling assumptions: one whole branch unit is one usable member of the required size (branch records have no length or diameter); one vine unit is 3 m of binding (the ex10 vine length law); one bark unit covers 0.5 m2 of overlapped roofing (the ex11 six-bark lean-to roof); ordinary '.' soil with waterlogging at most 0.1 permits hand insertion of forked posts to 0.3 m, and falling-object hazards and runoff channels are represented only by the ground type and waterlogging; the declared geometry is a 2 m ridge at 1.2 m over a 1 m deep floor, a slope of about 50 degrees; the material checks use the existing constitutive values probe reveals (branch strength 0.3, vine flexibility 0.9, bark water resistance 0.9) and the parts' current condition, so they fail only after wear; world wind has no direction, so the prevailing wind and wind-driven rain are taken to come from +x with a horizontal slant of 0.25 x wind per unit of fall, the convention of the existing ex10 open-refuge exposure solver; people have no wetness state in this world, so rain wetting is reduced through the rain part of the existing exposure chill; light weather means rain and wind at most 0.8, the frozen full-pressure rain amplitude of this scenario; protection scales with roof condition; with two or more people on the floor nobody is protected; only the builder may repair or dismantle because no access transfer is represented; posts are not separate collision bodies and the footprint is a reserved non-solid area; there is no dedicated viewer drawing, so the viewer's generic fallback shows the footprint colored by roof coverage. Reuse: collective-work.ts (escrow, paid work, stop), material-lots.ts, open-physical.ts (ground conditions and constitutive values), forest-climate.ts (rain, wind, outdoor chill), open-foundation.ts (personal records), the ex11 wear law and the ex10 wind-driven rain convention. Tests (apps/simulator/test/long-ex15-simple-shelter.test.ts, 11 cases, materials gathered by real gather actions) cover the ex15-only scope and four-round study, 12 rounds and 12 energy with per-increment installation and exact conservation and load transfer, measured shielding equal to the body-temperature difference against an unprotected copy with unchanged air temperature, satiety and energy, no wind protection with the open side to the wind, no protection for two occupants, off the floor or beyond the light-weather limits, pausing and resuming without charge, cancellation, rejected starts that spend nothing, builder-only rules, wear to unsafe followed by exact repair and reinspection, stage-by-stage dismantling and death. Development-3 was rejected by the handoff validator because the package declared its simple-shelter visual component before the viewer implemented it; this resubmission (development-4, a separate counted attempt) adds a small viewer drawing (footprint, ridge, installed roof courses, dashed until commissioned) and changes nothing else.

Two develop reviews at round 9, implemented in parallel. (1) Sol: Reviewed Sol's round-9 request 'Build a simple shared rain shelter' (a learnable, reusable small shelter from obtainable local materials with a resting area for Sol and others) and the World Agent's develop review (learning 4): the registry already holds simple-shelter@1, whose contract protects exactly one person, so develop a general 'Assemble and maintain a multi-bay rain shelter' operation as an occupancy and composition extension of that construction machinery, not a reinvention. Smallest shared version: two adjacent, independently braced lean-to bays, each with the inherited 2 m x 2 m footprint and 2 m x 1 m covered floor, reached from one unobstructed open side; 13 branch, 4 vine and 6 bark per bay (26, 8 and 12 for two), no stone, no tools; 12 one-energy increments per bay (24 for two), start pays only the first and an energy shortage pauses without charge; per-bay commissioning; at most one fitting occupant per bay, occupants of other bays never disable a bay and two in one bay void it; the inherited 50% rain and 35% wind chill reductions within rain and wind 0.8, with no stacking, nutrition, air-temperature or rest bonus; the inherited wear law and 0.5 sound threshold per bay; inspect one round and 0.2 energy; builder repair and dismantling; cancel and death rules; no refunds. The specification is self-consistent, so this is a simplified but real mechanism, not a first release. Implemented shared-shelter@1 (scope long-ex15, package dependencies foundation-open@1 and simple-shelter@1, handler long.shared-shelter, learning 4) with modes start, resume, cancel, inspect, repair and dismantle. Start takes x, y (footprint centre), orientation, bays (2-4, default 2) and exact owned untreated whole units of 13N branch, 4N vine and 6N bark (stone or any other extra is refused); it checks the whole 2 m x 2N m footprint (within reach of the first bay, inside the world, ordinary '.' soil sampled every 0.5 m, waterlogging at most 0.1, no hazard, no overlap with solid or reserved objects, no living person) and a 1 m deep approach strip along the shared open side (inside the world, no open water, no solid object, at least as deep as the widest living body); it creates one persistent object per bay (kind shared-shelter-bay, reserved non-solid 2 m x 2 m footprint, shared structure id, bay index) and reserves the materials through collective-work escrow as carried, owned pieces split per bay and increment with the inherited simple-shelter split. Each paid increment (one round, 1 energy; the bound start action continues) revalidates the reserved pieces, reach to the bay being built, its ground and that no other person stands in it, then moves that increment's pieces into the bay as installed components with the same quantity, origin and age. Bays are built one after another with the inherited plan (2 posts, 3 ridge and braces, 3 ribs and binding, 3 roofing courses, final check); each bay's twelfth increment runs the inherited lateral-stability, binding-pull, roof-load (8.4 mass units per bay) and runoff checks plus an open-approach check and commissions that bay alone, or leaves it unverified, while the next bay continues. Too little energy, leaving reach, another person in the bay being built or waterlogging pause without charge; a round not worked pauses; a lost reserved piece stops the work and returns the survivors. Cancel (one round, no energy) returns uninstalled pieces once, removes bays without parts, leaves partly built bays unfinished and keeps commissioned bays; death drops uninstalled pieces where the person died and leaves installed parts. Inspect (anyone who studied; one round, 0.2 energy; a bay in reach as target) reruns the checks for every bay of the structure in reach, which can withdraw or restore each bay's protection, and records an unverified personal record of each bay's parts, condition, coverage, status, last weather and occupants. Repair (builder only; one round, 1 energy) replaces one installed increment of one bay with the same recipe of owned units, leaving the removed parts on the ground with their condition; protection returns only after a passing reinspection. Dismantle (builder only; one round, 1 energy per stage) returns the last installed stage of one bay to the ground with each part's condition and leaves the other bays untouched. Effect: a new physiology hook (long-shared-shelter-exposure.ts, chained after the simple-shelter hook in forest-environment.ts and inactive unless shared-shelter@1 is installed, so ex7-ex15 saved rounds are unchanged) adds back exposure x (rain x rainShield + wind x windShield) of the existing outdoor exposure chill for a living person wholly on one commissioned bay's floor, with rainShield = 0.5 x that bay's roof condition x the body share whose wind-slanted rain ray meets that bay's roof plane and windShield = 0.35 x roof condition x max(0, cos(orientation)); occupancy is counted per bay, so two people on one floor void that bay only, people on other bays change nothing, and a body across the joint fits no floor; weather above 0.8, pooled water, the open side to the wind, an unfinished, unverified or unsafe bay, an enclosure, or a simple shelter already covering the body give no protection, and nothing stacks; air temperature, hunger, nutrition and rest are unchanged. Each round every installed part of every bay wears by 0.0005 + 0.002 x rain + 0.002 x wind, and a part below 0.5 makes only that bay unsafe. Events: shared-shelter-started, -progress, -paused, -resumed, -cancelled, -failed, -test-failed, -bay-commissioned, -inspected, -deteriorated, -damaged, -repaired, -dismantled, -occupancy (who now lies on each bay floor, with positions and whether its protection checks pass) and -exposure-measured (weather, outdoor and avoided chill, occupants, withheld reason and the leak measures exposedBodyShare and roofWear), all carrying the structure or bay id. Each bay's data.view keeps the inherited drawing metadata plus structure id, bay ids, structure footprint, orientation, open approach, installed-increment mask, frame and roof condition, roof coverage, commissioning status, actual occupant positions and the protected occupant (set only when that bay's coverage and weather checks pass); bays reuse the existing simple-shelter drawing (footprint, ridge, installed roof courses, dashed until commissioned), so no viewer change was needed. No satisfaction rule, comfort benefit, practice milestone or other reward is added. Modeling assumptions: the inherited simple-shelter ones (one branch unit is one usable member, one vine unit 3 m of binding, one bark unit 0.5 m2 of roofing; ordinary dry soil permits hand-set posts; the constitutive values probe reveals; wind and wind-driven rain from +x with a slant of 0.25 x wind; rain wetting is represented through the rain part of the exposure chill because people have no wetness state; light weather is rain and wind at most 0.8; protection scales with roof condition; posts are not collision bodies; only the builder may repair or dismantle); bays are adjacent along the ridge with no shared or spanning members, built strictly one after another, and each is commissioned on its own final increment; 2-4 bays are accepted because one bay is the existing simple shelter; the open approach is a 1 m deep strip along the whole open side that must be inside the world, free of open water and solid objects and at least as deep as the widest living body, checked at start and at every commissioning, while people and reserved non-solid areas do not block it; inspection covers every bay of the structure within the inspector's reach; occupancy is reported only when the set of people on a bay floor changes; the experience review's optional comfort benefit and maintained satisfaction were not added because the specification's effect is physical protection only; communication, travel, consent and other people's occupancy remain their own message, navigation and other actions, each paid by that person. Reuse: long-simple-shelter.ts (plan, allocation, split, installation, release, refresh, checks and wear constants, now exported without behavior change), long-shelter-exposure.ts (geometry, limits, floor test and roof-ray test, now exported, and the simple-shelter exposure for the no-stacking guard), collective-work.ts, material-lots.ts, open-physical.ts, forest-climate.ts and open-foundation.ts; probe, gather, pickup and message remain the separate existing operations. Tests (apps/simulator/test/long-ex15-shared-shelter.test.ts, 11 cases, materials gathered by real gather actions) cover the ex15-only scope and the simple-shelter@1 dependency, four-round study, 24 rounds and 24 energy with per-bay commissioning, exact conservation and load transfer, independent per-bay shielding equal to the body-temperature difference against an unprotected copy with unchanged air temperature, satiety and energy, a crowded bay losing protection while the other bay keeps it, no fit across the joint, no wind protection with the open side to the wind, withholding beyond the light-weather limits, pausing and resuming without charge (including an occupied bay), cancellation keeping a commissioned bay, rejected starts that spend nothing (one-bay recipe, stone substitution, wrong bay counts, bank soil, reach, a tree in the approach, an occupant, foreign materials, low energy), builder-only rules and inspection by others, wear disabling only the affected bay until exact repair and reinspection, per-bay stage-by-stage dismantling, and death. (2) Wren: Reviewed Wren's round-9 request 'Cultivate meadow roots' (a learnable, evidence-based way to plant or tend meadow roots so a finite food source can be replenished; a meadow-root patch visible near (10.1,12)) and the World Agent's develop review (learning 2): a general 'Establish and tend a cultivation trial' parameterized by source, exact owned propagule lot and quantity, reachable ground site and mode establish/tend/observe/resume/cancel/remove, with three one-round, one-energy establishment stages (prepare, place, cover and record), observation at the probe cost, tending at one round and one energy only with a supported intervention, irrigation only with real collected water, binding to the existing plant lifecycle and regeneration where present (an observation-only precursor otherwise), an 80-round inconclusive horizon, stalling or death from decay, drought, waterlogging or inadequate conditions, cancel, removal and death rules, harvest only through gather, and no benefit for requesting, studying or planting. Registry check: the long-ex15 registry (foundation-forest, foundation-open, foundation-expression, food-preparation@1, simple-shelter@1) has no planting operation; ex13 root-planting-trial@1 and ex14 cultivate-plant@1 are scoped to other experiments and are not modified. Unlike ex14's observation-only cultivate-plant@1, the existing ecology was checked first: under the development configuration open-ecology.ts already runs a conserved vegetative propagation lifecycle for non-woody plants (one parent stock unit becomes a seedling with stock 0, capacity min(4, parent capacity) and the parent's growth interval; it establishes once growth accumulated from actual temperature, light, soil moisture, season and waterlogging reaches 12, then regrows stock under the ordinary growth rule). The specification is therefore self-consistent and this is a simplified but real mechanism, not a first release. Implemented cultivation-trial@1 (scope long-ex15) with modes establish, resume, cancel, observe, tend and remove. Establish takes inputStackId (one whole owned unit; quantity must be 1), x, y and an optional target that must equal the unit's source. Before anything is spent it checks that the unit is a meadow-root unit, untreated (no drying, processing, combination or other represented treatment), unspoiled under the existing ageing law and gathered from a living root plant, and that the 0.25 m position is within reach, inside the world, on ordinary meadow soil (.) per the shared hand-preparation predicate, not standing water, waterlogging at most 0.1, soil moisture 0.3-1.2, at least 0.6 m from any object, clear of people, and with fewer than 3 root plants or unfinished trials within 5 m. It reserves the unit through collective-work escrow (still carried, owned and ageing) and runs three paid stages of one round and 1 energy each (establish pays the first and the bound action continues): prepare the position; place the unit (it leaves the inventory with its origin, mass and age, owned by nobody and reserved for the position, so it can no longer be eaten or planted elsewhere); cover and record (the position object becomes a seedling of the existing ecology: resource root, stock 0, capacity min(4, source capacity), the source's interval, establishment 0, one seed unit, its parent and the law's 600-round first-dispersal delay). Each stage rechecks reach, site, unit and energy: too little energy, leaving reach or a changed site pauses without charge, a round not worked pauses, and a lost or spoiled unit stops the work and returns survivors. After covering only ordinary simulation acts: the existing openPlants rule adds establishment from actual conditions, so cold, darkness, drought or waterlogging stall it; the buried unit keeps ageing under the existing food ageing law, and if it spoils before establishing the trial dies (interval set to 0, no further growth); when establishment completes the unit is absorbed (removed from the stacks, 1 unit and 0.4 mass recorded) and the position is an ordinary meadow-root plant whose stock regrows only under the existing growth rule, is harvested by anyone through gather at its existing cost, and may later disperse under the same law. At 80 planted rounds without establishing or dying the record reports 'inconclusive' and nothing else changes. Observe (anyone who studied; a trial or plant source in reach) runs the baseline probe observation (one round, 0.2 energy) and, for a trial, stores an unverified personal record of only visible state (lifecycle, elapsed rounds, visible stock, whether it sprouted, the unit's condition only while uncovered, soil and weather) and appends to the trial's observation log; monitoring an existing patch takes no food and adds no plant; information gain is only the probe's existing evidence-deduplicated change finding. Tend is refused with nothing spent because no supported intervention is represented (no competing plant can stand within the 0.6 m spacing, soil displacement is not represented, and no water collection or delivery exists for irrigation). Cancel (one round, no energy) returns an unplaced unit once and leaves a placed unit uncovered in the position, where it does not establish and eventually rots. Remove (planter only, one round, 1 energy) returns an uncovered or covered unit in its current condition, returns nothing for a dead trial and clears the position; it is refused for an established plant (no uprooting rule; harvest with gather). Death drops an unplaced unit where the person died and leaves placed or planted units to the ecology. Nothing spent is refunded. Events: cultivation-position-prepared, cultivation-unit-placed, cultivation-planted, cultivation-work-paused, -resumed, -cancelled and -failed, cultivation-trial-observed, cultivation-patch-observed, cultivation-trial-established, -died, -harvested and -removed. The object's data.view holds the trial id, source and lot, site bounds, quantity placed, stages completed, lifecycle, observation ticks and last observation, whether the unit is visible, and verified harvestable stock; a new small viewer drawing (cultivation-trial) shows a dashed soil position while worked, the unit only while uncovered, a covered mound with nothing visible while planted, a sprout with stock dots only after establishment and a withered mark when dead, and plants later dispersed from a trial fall back to the ordinary plant drawing. No satisfaction rule, practice milestone (cultivation-planted carries no qualified flag) or other reward is added. Modeling assumptions: meadow roots are the only supported species, because the existing propagation law treats one root stock unit as a vegetative propagule and the harvested organ is that unit; a harvested root unit stays viable exactly while it is whole, untreated and unspoiled under the existing ageing law, with no separate viability clock; only a covered unit establishes, so an uncovered placed unit never does; hand preparation is limited to ordinary meadow soil (.), the shared ex13/ex14 predicate, so forest floor (where the (10.1,12) patch grows) needs a different site; the position's area is the existing root plant footprint (radius 0.25) and depth is not represented; the site conditions are those under which the existing dispersal law starts a plant (soil moisture 0.3-1.2, 0.6 m spacing, fewer than 3 same-resource plants within 5 m), extended to count unfinished trials; a planted trial has the same capacity, interval, establishment threshold, growth, waterlogging, seasonal and dispersal behavior as a naturally dispersed seedling of its source; the unit is absorbed into the plant at establishment, as a dispersed parent stock unit is; the position object has createdBy null like every plant, so observers see only public plant fields (the growth interval and dispersal schedule stay hidden) and the planter is kept in the trial record for planter-only removal; quantity is exactly one unit; harvest debits stock at gather's existing cost.
